**What it includes:**

- **HTML** — a header, an input form for adding todos, filter buttons (All / Active / Completed), the todo list, and an items-left footer with a "Clear completed" action.
- **CSS** — clean modern styling: gradient background, card container, strikethrough + muted color for completed items, active filter button highlighting, and responsive/mobile-friendly layout.
- **JS** — vanilla JavaScript with:
  - **Add** — submit the form (Enter key) to add a todo; empty input is ignored.
  - **Toggle complete** — click a checkbox to mark done; completed items get strikethrough styling.
  - **Delete** — a delete button on each row removes the todo.
  - **Filter** — All / Active / Completed tabs re-render the visible list; counts shown.
  - **Persistence** — the full todo array (text + completed flag) is saved to `localStorage` on every change and restored on page load via `loadState()`/`saveState()`.

No external dependencies — just open the file in any browser.

{"path":"todo_zai-glm-5.3-flash_01.html","edit_description":"Create a brand-new single self-contained HTML file "todo_zai-glm-5.3-flash_01.html" containing a complete Todo app with ALL HTML, CSS, and JavaScript inline (no external dependencies, no CDN links, works offline by double-clicking the file).

Required functionality (must all work):
1. Add new todos: a text input with placeholder "What needs to be done?" plus an "Add" button; adding works both via the button click and by pressing Enter in the input. Empty/whitespace-only input is ignored. After adding, the input is cleared and refocused. New todos are prepended or appended to the list consistently.
2. Mark todos as complete: each todo row has a checkbox; checking it applies a line-through strikethrough style and a muted/grayed color to the todo text; unchecking restores it.
3. Delete todos: each todo row has a "Delete" (or ×) button that removes that todo immediately.
4. Filters: three filter buttons — All / Active / Completed. "All" shows every todo, "Active" shows only unchecked todos, "Completed" shows only checked ones. The currently active filter button is visually highlighted. Switching filters re-renders the list; the filter selection should also persist to localStorage so it survives reloads.
5. localStorage persistence: todos are saved to localStorage (JSON array of {id, text, completed}) under a key like "todos_zai" on every change (add, toggle, delete), and loaded on page load so the list survives refresh. Wrap localStorage access in try/catch so the app still works if storage is unavailable.

Also include nice-to-have polish:
- A footer/status line showing "N items left" (count of active todos).
- A "Clear completed" button that removes all completed todos (hidden or disabled when there are none).
- An empty-state message (e.g. "No todos yet" / "Nothing active" / "Nothing completed") when the filtered list is empty.
- Escape key in the input clears it.

Styling requirements:
- Clean, modern look: system font stack, centered card container (max-width ~520px) with rounded corners and a subtle box shadow on a soft background (e.g. light gray-blue gradient or #f4f5f7).
- Filter buttons styled as a segmented control (pill/rounded group), active filter highlighted with accent color (e.g. #4f6df5 or similar indigo).
- Checked todo rows show line-through text with reduced opacity; hover states on delete button (red tint) and list rows.
- Smooth, subtle transitions on hover; adequate padding, spacing, and contrast. Responsive enough to look fine on narrow screens.
- Use plain semantic HTML (input, ul/li, button), an <h1> title like "Todos", and keep everything in ONE file: <style> in <head>, <script> at end of <body> (or defer), with "use strict", no frameworks, no libraries.

Code quality: use a single render() function that re-renders the list from state, event delegation or per-item listeners is fine, ids generated via Date.now()+random or a counter persisted counter. No console errors."}
